common.title: Model Explorer
common.lead: The object model of the board as a live tree, with the globals you can edit, watch, save and keep across reboots.

model.rrf_chip_help: Firmware of the board. Global variables need RepRapFirmware 3.4 or newer.
model.report_help: Builds a text with the firmware, boards, versions, plugins, sensors, drivers, network state, heaters, volumes and the active warnings, ready to paste into the Duet forum or a GitHub issue. Addresses, names, serial numbers and file paths are left out unless you tick them; user names and passwords are never read. Without it you have to collect these facts by hand from several pages. Press Build report, read it, then copy or download it.
model.report_private: Private data, left out unless you tick it
model.report_copy_failed: The browser did not allow copying. Select the text and copy it by hand.
model.report_download_failed: The browser did not allow the download.
model.report_empty: Nothing built yet. Press Build report.
model.report_stale: You changed a tick box: build the report again.
model.export_help: Downloads the watched values as CSV or JSON with ISO time stamps and one column per path: numbers as numbers, booleans as true and false, texts with their value from the moment they changed. The changes of the Changes view can be downloaded too. Without it the values only live on the screen and in this browser. Pick a range, then a button.
model.export_none: Nothing is watched yet: add paths to the watch list first.
model.export_summary: {rows} rows, {paths} paths, {changes} changes in the range.
model.export_failed: The browser did not allow the download.
model.alerts_help: Limits on any path of the model: a number over or under a limit, a value equal to a word, or a change to a word. When one fires, a banner appears at the top of the page and the event is listed here. Without alerts you must keep looking at the values yourself. Add a rule below.
model.alerts_scope: They only work while this page is open in a browser. Nothing runs on the Pi and nothing is sent to a phone: close the page and the alerts stop.
model.alerts_invalid: Give a path and a limit (a number for above and below, a word for the others).
model.alerts_events_none: Nothing has fired since the page opened.
model.macromap_help: For each macro file read by the scan: the parameters it reads with their guards and defaults, the globals it reads, writes or defines, the macros it calls with M98 and what it passes them, and one line showing how to call it. Square brackets in the example mark optional parameters. Scan first; the map is built from the same files.
model.macromap_dynamic: the file is built at run time: {expr}
model.macromap_aborts: Can stop with abort at line {lines}.
model.macromap_none: No macro files have been read yet. Read the files first.
model.report_inc_name_what: The name you gave the machine in config.g with M550.
model.report_inc_name_why: Support people sometimes want it to tell machines apart in a thread.
model.report_inc_name_missing: The report says nothing about the name; everything else is still there.
model.report_inc_name_help: Tick it only if you are happy to share the name.
model.report_inc_hostname_what: The network name of the board or of the Pi.
model.report_inc_hostname_why: It helps when a network problem depends on how the machine is named.
model.report_inc_hostname_missing: The report does not show it; the network state is still listed.
model.report_inc_hostname_help: Tick it only if it holds nothing personal.
model.report_inc_ip_what: The address, the gateway and the subnet of each network interface.
model.report_inc_ip_why: Needed only to debug a network setup in detail.
model.report_inc_ip_missing: The report shows the interface, its state and its speed without any address.
model.report_inc_ip_help: Leave it off when posting in public; tick it when someone you trust asks.
model.report_inc_mac_what: The hardware address of each network interface.
model.report_inc_mac_why: It identifies one network card and a few network problems depend on it.
model.report_inc_mac_missing: The report does not show it.
model.report_inc_mac_help: Leave it off unless support asks for it.
model.report_inc_serial_what: The unique ID that each board reports.
model.report_inc_serial_why: Needed when a problem concerns one particular board, for example a warranty or a license.
model.report_inc_serial_missing: The report shows the board model and firmware without the serial number.
model.report_inc_serial_help: Leave it off unless the seller or support asks for it.
model.report_inc_paths_what: The name of the job file and the folders of the machine.
model.report_inc_paths_why: It shows where files live when a problem is about a missing or misplaced file.
model.report_inc_paths_missing: The report shows nothing about files or folders.
model.report_inc_paths_help: File names can say a lot about you: tick it only when it is needed.
model.report_dwc_what: The version of Duet Web Control that shows this page.
model.report_dwc_why: Many display problems depend on it and the board cannot report it.
model.report_dwc_missing: The report says that DWC was not detected.
model.report_dwc_help: Type it as shown in the DWC settings under About if the field is empty.
model.export_range_what: How far back from now the export goes.
model.export_range_why: To take only the last minutes of an event instead of everything the page holds.
model.export_range_missing: Everything the page holds is exported.
model.export_range_help: Pick a range, then a download button. The page holds the last 300 samples of each path.
model.alerts_set_path_what: The value of the model to watch, such as heat.heaters[0].current.
model.alerts_set_path_why: An alert needs one value to compare.
model.alerts_set_path_missing: A rule without a path cannot work and is not saved.
model.alerts_set_path_help: Type the path, or pick one of your watched paths. The Model section can copy any path.
model.alerts_set_op_what: The kind of test: goes above a number, goes below a number, is equal to a word, or changes to a word.
model.alerts_set_op_why: A temperature needs a limit; a status word needs a match.
model.alerts_set_op_missing: A value can only be tested the ways in the list.
model.alerts_set_op_help: Above and below need a number. Is equal to stays firing while the value matches. Changes to fires once each time the value becomes that word.
model.alerts_set_value_what: The number to compare with, or the word to match, such as idle, halted or true.
model.alerts_set_value_why: It is what the path is compared with.
model.alerts_set_value_help: Type a number for above and below, a word for the other two. A boolean is true or false.
model.alerts_set_hysteresis_what: How far back past the limit the value must go before the alert counts as over.
model.alerts_set_hysteresis_why: A value that wobbles around the limit would fire again and again.
model.alerts_set_hysteresis_missing: With 0 the alert is over as soon as the value touches the limit again and may fire many times.
model.alerts_set_hysteresis_help: For a limit of 100 and hysteresis 5, an alert above 100 ends at 95 or lower. Only for above and below.
model.alerts_set_cooldown_what: The shortest time between two alerts of the same rule.
model.alerts_set_cooldown_why: So a noisy value does not fill the banner and the list.
model.alerts_set_cooldown_missing: With 0 every new crossing fires at once.
model.alerts_set_cooldown_help: 60 is a good start. A limit still crossed when the time is over fires then.
model.alerts_set_sound_what: Two short tones when an alert fires.
model.alerts_set_sound_why: To hear an alert while you look at the machine and not at the screen.
model.alerts_set_sound_missing: Alerts show only as a banner and in the list. The sound is off by default.
model.alerts_set_sound_help: Turn it on and touch the page once: the browser keeps a page silent until then. It only sounds while this page is open.
model.macromap_view_what: For each macro file: the parameters it reads, the globals it uses, the macros it calls and how to call it.
model.macromap_view_why: To know what to pass to a macro and what may break if you change one.
model.macromap_view_missing: You have to open every macro to find out.
model.macromap_view_help: Scan first, then search by file, param.S, a global or a macro name, and open a row for the details.
model.tier_help_on: SBC mode with DSF {version}: the extras are on, done by this page from DWC with no plugin on the Pi (the watch history is also saved in 0:/sys/workshop-model-watch.json, the usage finder reads more files, the sbc and plugins branches are shown).
model.tier_off_no_sbc: Standalone Duet: the SBC extras are off (the watch history stays in this browser and the usage finder reads fewer files). Everything else works the same.
model.tier_off_no_dsf: SBC without DSF data yet: the SBC extras stay off until DSF reports its version.
model.tier_off_old_dsf: DSF {version} is older than {minimum}: the SBC extras stay off. Everything else works the same.
model.tier_off_no_plugin_support: DSF reports no plugin support: the SBC extras stay off. Everything else works the same.
model.companion_running: The companion plugin WorkshopModelAgent is running on the Pi.
model.reason_globals_off: RRF {version} is older than {minimum}: the globals features are off
model.tree_help: The object model of the board, refreshed once a second. Pick how to look at it: by topic, as a flat list or as the technical tree.
model.tree_truncated: The tree is cut at {n} rows: close some branches to see the rest.
model.detail_none: Tap a row of the tree to see its value, copy its path or watch it.
model.snippets_help: Snippets to paste in a macro, a panel or the console.
model.globals_help: The global variables of the board, in groups by the start of their name. Search, filter and sort them, change a number or a switch in place, and use the menu of a row for the rest.
model.globals_off_rrf: This board runs RRF {version}; global variables need {minimum} or newer, so the globals features are off. The tree, the watch list and the path helper work.
model.globals_off_unknown: The board has not reported its firmware version yet: the globals features wait for it.
model.globals_none: No global exists yet. Create one below, or define it in config.g.
model.create_help: A new variable the macros and panels can read. Pick its type and write the value; the exact command is shown before it is sent.
model.edit_value_hint_array: values separated by commas, texts in quotes
model.edit_value_hint_expression: an RRF expression, sent as written
model.err_name: The name needs letters, digits or underscore and cannot start with a digit.
model.err_array_item: Each item of the array must be a number, true, false or a text in quotes.
model.err_array_empty: The array needs at least one value.
model.read_only: Your role can read the globals but not change them.
model.persist_help: The plugin writes its value in the persistence macro; config.g has to call that macro.
model.persist_text: RepRapFirmware forgets every global when it restarts. The globals you mark are written to one macro the plugin generates; add the line below to config.g, after the hardware is configured, and they come back at boot.
model.persist_none: No global is kept yet. Mark one with the switch of its editor. The macro would be
model.persist_include_missing: config.g does not call the macro yet: add this line to config.g.
model.persist_include_unknown: config.g could not be read: check that it calls
model.persist_update_help: Rewrites the macro with the value each kept global has right now.
model.cannot_delete_text: RepRapFirmware cannot delete a global until the next reboot: there is no delete button on purpose. To forget one, remove it from the macros that create it and restart the board.
model.preview_slow: The board has not answered in 15 s.
model.preview_level1: {n} lines, sent with one tap: they only change values that can be set back.
model.preview_level2: {n} lines, one of them is a G or M code that may move the machine or heat: it needs two taps.
model.watch_help: Pin any path (a global, a sensor, a position) from the tree and see its value, its minimum and maximum and a small line of the last samples, one per second.
model.watch_none: Nothing watched yet. Open a row in the tree and tap Watch.
model.watch_saved_sbc: The list and its samples are saved in this browser and, with the SBC tier, in 0:/sys/workshop-model-watch.json every 30 s, so another device resumes them.
model.watch_saved_browser: The list and its samples are saved in this browser (standalone Duet: no file is written for them).
model.changes_help: What changed in the globals and the watched paths, newest first, with the value before and after.
model.presets_help: A preset is a named copy of all the globals. Save the current values, compare a preset with the machine, apply it, export it as a file or import one. The presets live in
model.preset_save_help: Saves the {n} globals the board has right now under that name (a preset with the same name is replaced).
model.preset_export_failed: The file could not be downloaded.
model.preset_nothing_to_apply: The machine already has these values.
model.usage_help: Reads the macros on the SD card and tells you which globals have a problem, which ones to check and where each one is used.
model.usage_budget: Up to {files} files of {kb} KB each are read.
model.usage_budget_standalone: On a standalone Duet the files come through the board, so the budget is small.
model.view_selector_label: How to look at the model
model.view_topics_what: One card per area of the machine (state, temperatures, axes, job, tools, fans, sensors, boards, network, plugins, globals) with readable names, units and live values.
model.view_topics_why: To read the state of the machine at a glance without knowing the names of the object model.
model.view_topics_missing: You read the technical tree: every key with its firmware name and no units.
model.view_topics_help: Tap a row to open it in the technical tree; See all opens the whole branch of the card. The keys no card covers are in Other.
model.view_flat_what: Every value of the model in one table: path, value and type.
model.view_flat_why: To find, filter and sort values: only numbers, only what changed in the last minute, only what you watch.
model.view_flat_missing: You open branch after branch to find a value.
model.view_flat_help: Write in the filter to search the path and the value, tap the type pills, tap a column head to sort. Tap a row to see its detail on the right.
model.view_tree_what: The object model as the firmware writes it, branch by branch, with the search by key and value.
model.view_tree_why: For macros and panels: the exact path of a value, the snippets to copy and the editor of globals.
model.view_tree_missing: You do not see the exact paths to use in a macro.
model.view_tree_help: Open a branch with its arrow, tap a row to see its detail on the right, then copy the path or a snippet.
model.topics_none: The model of the board has not arrived yet.
model.topic_other_help: Keys no card covers. Tap one to open it in the technical tree.
model.topic_global_off: Global variables need RRF 3.4 or newer.
model.flat_truncated: The model has more than {n} values: only the first ones are listed.
model.scope_all_what: Every value of the object model at this moment.
model.scope_all_why: To compare the whole machine before and after a change: a new config.g, a firmware update, a job.
model.scope_all_missing: You keep only one branch, and a change somewhere else goes unnoticed.
model.scope_all_help: Write a name and tap Save snapshot. Compare it later with another snapshot or with the model now.
model.scope_branch_what: Only the values under one path you pick here: a search by name, a favourite, a part used before or what is selected in the Model section.
model.scope_branch_why: Small and focused: the heaters, the axes or the globals, without the clock values that change every second.
model.scope_branch_missing: You keep the whole model, bigger and with values that change all the time.
model.scope_branch_help: Tap a chip or search a branch (heat, move.axes, global), read what will be saved, then Save snapshot.
model.tester_echo_what: Any RRF expression, sent with echo, which prints its value.
model.tester_echo_why: To check what a condition or a calculation of a macro gives on this machine right now, without writing a macro.
model.tester_echo_missing: You find out only when the macro runs.
model.tester_echo_help: Write it as in a macro, for example move.axes[0].machinePosition + 1 or #tools, then tap Send. It only reads: a line that starts with > (writing a file) is refused.
model.tester_m409_what: A path of the object model, read with M409, which answers in JSON.
model.tester_m409_why: To see a node exactly as the firmware reports it, with everything inside.
model.tester_m409_missing: You read the copy DWC keeps, which may lag behind the board.
model.tester_m409_help: Write a path such as heat.heaters[1] or global and tap Send; a branch is read whole.
model.snapshots_help: A snapshot keeps every value of the model, or of one branch, under a name: compare two moments, or a moment with now. They are saved in
model.snapshot_scope_none: Pick a part of the model first.
model.snapshot_truncated: Only the first {n} values were kept (the budget of this machine).
model.snapshot_budget: This machine keeps up to {count} snapshots of up to {leaves} values each; the oldest goes when a new one does not fit.
model.snapshot_budget_standalone: On a standalone Duet the file goes through the board, so the budget is small.
model.snapshot_export_failed: The file could not be downloaded.
model.compare_help: Pick two snapshots, or a snapshot and the model now, and see what changed between them.
model.compare_same: Both sides are the same: pick two different ones.
model.tester_help: Write an expression or a path and see what the board answers, right here. The command only reads; it goes through the command preview with one tap.
model.tester_err_redirect: An expression cannot start with > (that would write a file).
model.tester_err_not_path: M409 needs a path of the model, like heat.heaters[1].
model.tester_result_error: The board answered with an error:
model.tester_offline: Connect to the board to test.
model.test_in_tester_help: Open this path in the expression tester
model.detail_table_more_cols: {n} more columns: open a row to see them all
model.view_columns_what: The model as columns, like a file browser: a key you pick opens its keys in the next column.
model.view_columns_why: To walk down a branch and still see every level above it, side by side.
model.view_columns_missing: You open and close branches of one long tree and lose sight of where you are.
model.view_columns_help: Tap a key to open the next column; the arrow keys move and Left goes up a level. The bar above copies, watches, pins or opens the selected path in the technical tree.
model.view_browse_what: One level of the model at a time, with the path on top and a Back button.
model.view_browse_why: To explore the model step by step, like the folders of a phone, without a long tree.
model.view_browse_missing: You see every level at once in the technical tree.
model.view_browse_help: Tap a branch to open it and a value to see its detail on the right. Back returns to where you were, Up goes to the level above and the path on top jumps to any level. Filter and sort the keys of the level.
model.view_changes_what: Only the values that changed since a moment you pick, with the value at that moment and the value now.
model.view_changes_why: To see what a macro, a command or a job changed in the machine without reading the whole model.
model.view_changes_missing: You compare values from memory or watch one changing row at a time.
model.view_changes_help: Press Mark, do what you want to check and read what changed. Or compare with the moment this view opened, or with the last 10 seconds, minute or 5 minutes. Filter by path and by kind of change, and hide what changes all the time.
model.kind_number_special: number that is not finite: NaN or infinity
model.pin_full: The favourites are full ({n}): remove one to add another
model.pins_empty: Tap the star of a value to keep it here.
model.pins_gone: {path} is not in the model now
model.pins_row_what: A short list of paths you keep at hand, with their live values, at the top of the Model section.
model.pins_row_why: To reach the values you check often in one tap, from any view.
model.pins_row_missing: You look for the same values again every time.
model.pins_row_help: Tap the star next to a value in any view. Tap a favourite to select it, the tree icon to open it in the technical tree and the cross to remove it. The list is kept in this browser.
model.density_comfortable_what: Taller rows with more space between them.
model.density_comfortable_why: Easier to read and to tap on a touch screen.
model.density_comfortable_missing: The rows are tight and harder to hit with a finger.
model.density_comfortable_help: Pick it on the kiosk or a tablet. The choice is kept in this browser.
model.density_compact_what: Shorter rows, more of them on the screen.
model.density_compact_why: To see more values at once on a big screen.
model.density_compact_missing: Fewer rows fit and you scroll more.
model.density_compact_help: Pick it on a computer with a mouse. The choice is kept in this browser.
model.columns_help: Pick a key and its keys open in the next column. The arrow keys move; Left goes up a level.
model.columns_truncated: This branch has {n} keys: only the first ones are listed.
model.columns_missing: {path} is not in the model now.
model.browse_help: Tap a branch to go in and a value to see its detail. Back returns; Up goes one level up.
model.browse_back_none: Nothing to go back to yet
model.browse_up_none: This is the top of the model
model.browse_sort_model_what: The keys in the order the firmware writes them.
model.browse_sort_model_why: Related keys stay together, as in the documentation of the object model.
model.browse_sort_model_missing: You only get the alphabetical or the grouped order.
model.browse_sort_model_help: It is the default; the buttons next to it pick another order.
model.browse_sort_name_what: The keys from A to Z, the list positions by number.
model.browse_sort_name_why: To find a key whose name you know.
model.browse_sort_name_missing: You read the whole level to find a name.
model.browse_sort_name_help: Tap Name. Numbers inside a key count as numbers: 2 comes before 10.
model.browse_sort_kind_what: The keys grouped by type: numbers, texts, booleans, lists, objects, nulls and colours.
model.browse_sort_kind_why: To see the branches apart from the values, or all the numbers together.
model.browse_sort_kind_help: Tap Type; inside each type the keys go by name.
model.browse_gone: {path} is not in the model now. Go back, or tap Model on top.
model.browse_truncated: This level has {n} keys: only the first ones are listed.
model.changes_view_help: What changed since the moment you pick: the value then and the value now.
model.changes_since_mark_what: The values as they were when you pressed Mark.
model.changes_since_mark_why: To see exactly what one action changed: press Mark, act, read.
model.changes_since_mark_missing: Older changes mix with the ones you want to see.
model.changes_since_mark_help: Press Mark just before the action; press it again to start over from that moment.
model.changes_since_open_what: The values as they were when this view opened, or when you last pressed Clear.
model.changes_since_open_why: To review everything that changed while you were here.
model.changes_since_open_missing: You only see a short window of time.
model.changes_since_open_help: Clear starts this moment again from now.
model.changes_since_s10_what: What changed in the last 10 seconds.
model.changes_since_s10_why: To follow what is moving right now.
model.changes_since_s10_missing: Changes from long ago stay in the list.
model.changes_since_s10_help: The window moves with the clock: a value leaves the list 10 seconds after its last change.
model.changes_since_m1_what: What changed in the last minute.
model.changes_since_m1_why: To check the effect of something you just did.
model.changes_since_m1_missing: You read changes of a time you are not looking at.
model.changes_since_m1_help: The window moves with the clock: a value leaves the list a minute after its last change.
model.changes_since_m5_what: What changed in the last 5 minutes.
model.changes_since_m5_why: To review a short task, such as heating up or homing.
model.changes_since_m5_missing: You only see the last minute, or everything since the view opened.
model.changes_since_m5_help: The window moves with the clock. Very busy machines can keep fewer than 5 minutes of changes.
model.changes_mark_help: Remember every value as it is now and show only what changes after this
model.changes_mark_none: No mark yet: press Mark to compare from now on.
model.changes_clear_help: Forget the changes recorded until now
model.changes_status_changed_why: The main answer: what is not as it was.
model.changes_status_changed_missing: You see every kind of change together.
model.changes_status_changed_help: Tap it to show only these; tap it again to show every kind.
model.changes_status_added_what: Values that were not in the model at that moment.
model.changes_status_added_why: A new tool, sensor, global or message shows up here.
model.changes_status_added_missing: New values mix with the ones that changed.
model.changes_status_added_help: Tap it to show only these; tap it again to show every kind.
model.changes_status_removed_what: Values that were in the model and are not any more.
model.changes_status_removed_why: A board that went away or a list that emptied shows up here.
model.changes_status_removed_missing: You do not notice what disappeared.
model.changes_status_removed_help: Tap it to show only these; tap it again to show every kind.
model.changes_status_back_what: Values that changed and returned to what they were.
model.changes_status_back_why: A switch that went on and off, or a short jump of a reading.
model.changes_status_back_missing: A value that moved and came back goes unnoticed.
model.changes_status_back_help: Tap it to show only these; tap it again to show every kind.
model.changes_hide_frequent: Hide what changes all the time
model.changes_hide_frequent_what: Hides the values that changed at least 5 times, about every 2 seconds or faster, such as the uptime or a live temperature.
model.changes_hide_frequent_why: So the values that matter are not buried under the ones that always move.
model.changes_hide_frequent_help: Turn it off to see everything; the line above says how many are hidden.
model.changes_paused: Sampling is paused: nothing new is recorded until you resume.
model.changes_count_hidden: Values in the list: {n}; {hidden} that change all the time are hidden
model.changes_waiting: Waiting for the first sample of the model.
model.watch_markers_what: A dot on the line of a number wherever it jumped much more than it usually moves.
model.watch_markers_why: To find at a glance the moment a temperature, a position or a reading jumped.
model.watch_markers_missing: The lines are drawn without dots; a jump is still in the line and in the changes of the row.
model.watch_markers_help: Turn it on and look for the dots on the lines; open the changes of the row for the time and the values.
model.watch_bands_label: Timeline of the values of the last minutes
model.changes_hide_noise_what: Hides the command logs other plugins keep (paths under lastCommands) and time stamps that move every second.
model.changes_hide_noise_why: So the list shows the changes of the machine and not the bookkeeping of other plugins.
model.changes_hide_noise_missing: Those paths fill the list and push the real changes down.
model.changes_hide_noise_help: On by default. Tap the chip with the count to show them again, and tap it again to hide them.
model.usage_set_chain_what: config.g, every file it runs with M98 (and the files those run), daemon.g and start.g.
model.usage_set_chain_why: These are the files that really run on this machine, so their globals are the ones that matter.
model.usage_set_chain_missing: Only the folders below are read; a macro called from config.g that lives elsewhere is missed.
model.usage_set_chain_help: Leave it on. A file reached twice is read once, and a loop of M98 calls stops by itself.
model.usage_set_folder_what: The folders whose .g files are read besides the chain of config.g: the top of 0:/macros by default, and every folder found inside.
model.usage_set_folder_why: Macros started from the DWC buttons, from a panel or by hand live in 0:/macros and are not called from config.g.
model.usage_set_folder_missing: The globals those macros use are not counted and can show up as unused.
model.usage_set_folder_help: Tick the folders to read. The folders found inside appear here after the first scan; the choice is kept in this browser.
model.usage_set_depth_what: How many levels of folders are opened: 1 reads only the files at the top of each folder, 2 also one level of subfolders.
model.usage_set_depth_why: A small depth keeps the scan quick and leaves out deep archives of old macros.
model.usage_set_depth_missing: With depth 1 the macros kept in subfolders are not read.
model.usage_set_depth_help: 2 is the default. Raise it only when your macros live deeper.
model.usage_set_hide: Leave out backups, examples and plugin folders
model.usage_set_hide_what: Skips files and folders named like a backup (bak, backup, old), the examples, and the folders of installed plugins.
model.usage_set_hide_why: Old copies and examples repeat the same globals and fill the result with noise.
model.usage_set_hide_missing: Every copy is read and its globals are counted again.
model.usage_set_hide_help: On by default. Turn it off to see what an old copy or a plugin folder uses.
model.usage_folder_excluded: left out: backup, example or plugin
model.usage_result: {read} files read, {cached} unchanged since the last scan, {skipped} left out by the budget.
model.usage_cache_sbc: Files that did not change are not read again; in SBC mode the memory of the last scan is kept in the watch file.
model.usage_cache_browser: Files that did not change are not read again while this page is open (standalone Duet: nothing is written for it).
model.usage_hint_help: A plugin, a panel of DWC or the console may read it: it is only a hint, not an error.
model.usage_search_hint: a global or a file name
model.globals_set_persistent_what: Shows only the globals written in the persistence macro.
model.globals_set_persistent_why: To check at a glance what comes back after a restart.
model.globals_set_persistent_help: Mark a global as kept from its editor; the panel below says when the saved value is not the live one.
model.globals_set_changed_what: Shows only the globals whose value changed in the last minute while this page was open.
model.globals_set_changed_why: To see what a macro or a job is changing right now.
model.globals_set_changed_missing: Every global is listed, whether it moves or not.
model.globals_set_changed_help: Leave the page open while the macro runs; sort by last change to see the newest first.
model.globals_set_watched_what: Shows only the globals in the watch list.
model.globals_set_watched_why: To keep the few that matter in front of you.
model.globals_set_watched_help: Add a global to the watch list from the menu of its row.
model.globals_set_sort_what: The order of the globals inside each group: name, type or the newest change first. Favourites always come first.
model.globals_set_sort_why: Name to find one, type to compare alike values, last change to follow what moves.
model.globals_set_sort_missing: The globals keep the order of the name.
model.globals_set_sort_help: Pick the order here; the star of a row makes it a favourite that stays on top.
model.globals_set_quick_what: A switch for a boolean and a stepper for a number, right in the card.
model.globals_set_quick_why: Most changes are a flag or a number: no need to open the full editor for them.
model.globals_set_quick_missing: Every change goes through Edit in the menu of the row.
model.globals_set_quick_help: Flip the switch, or tap - and + (or write the number and press Enter); the exact command appears under the card and goes with one tap. Other types use Edit in the menu.
model.globals_used_help: Files that use it, from the last scan of the usage finder
model.persist_panel_ok: {n} kept, every saved value matches the live one.
model.persist_attention_stale: {n} kept globals have another value now: save the current values, or leave the saved ones for the next boot.
model.persist_attention_include: config.g does not call the macro: the kept globals are not restored at boot.
model.usage_maybe_help: A file reads it and none of the files read creates it, but some folders that could create it were not read. Read them to be sure.
model.builder_paths_what: Every path of the live model of this board, with its type and value now, to put in the expression.
model.builder_paths_why: To write a path without remembering or mistyping it.
model.builder_paths_missing: You type the paths by hand and a typo shows up only as an error from the board.
model.builder_paths_help: Search by a word or a part of a path, tap a row to put it where the cursor is, or the arrow to go down one level.
model.builder_catalog_what: Everything an RRF expression can do, in groups, with an explanation and an example each.
model.builder_catalog_why: To find the operator or the function you need and put its pattern in the expression.
model.builder_catalog_missing: You look it up in the firmware documentation every time.
model.builder_catalog_help: Pick a group or search, tap Insert: the pattern goes where the cursor is and the first blank, written between < and >, is selected so you type over it. What this firmware does not have is hidden.
model.builder_recipes_what: Ready expressions for the workshop, built with the real paths of this machine.
model.builder_recipes_why: To start from something that already works here and change it.
model.builder_recipes_missing: You start from a blank field.
model.builder_recipes_help: Tap Load: the expression replaces the field. Change the numbers or the paths, then evaluate it.
model.builder_saved_what: The expressions you keep, remembered in this browser.
model.builder_saved_why: To come back to an expression you use often without writing it again.
model.builder_saved_missing: You lose it when you leave, except what is in the short history of this visit.
model.builder_saved_help: Tap the star under the field to keep the current expression; tap Load to bring one back.
model.pick_search: Search a path or a value
model.pick_cursor_none: Put the cursor on a path of the expression to see its value now.
model.pick_cursor_missing: {path} is not in the model now.
model.catalog_search: Search (a word, a function, an example)
model.catalog_gcode_note: A line of a macro, not an expression: it cannot be tested here, only copied.
model.catalog_unknown: The board has not told its version yet.
model.catalog_hidden: {n} entries need a newer firmware than this board has and are hidden.
model.expr_minus: Subtracts the second number from the first.
model.expr_divide: Divides the first number by the second.
model.expr_equal: True when both sides are equal; works on numbers, text and booleans.
model.expr_not_equal: True when the two sides are different.
model.expr_compare: Compares numbers; also less than, greater than and less or equal.
model.expr_and: True only when both conditions are true.
model.expr_or: True when at least one condition is true.
model.expr_not: Turns true into false and false into true.
model.expr_ternary: Chooses between two values: the first when the condition is true, the second when it is not.
model.expr_parens: Parentheses decide what is calculated first.
model.expr_concat: Joins two values into one text; a number is turned into text.
model.expr_text: A text goes between double quotes; write two quotes to put one quote inside.
model.expr_floor: Rounds down to a whole number.
model.expr_ceil: Rounds up to a whole number.
model.expr_round: Rounds to one decimal (there is no round function: this is the usual trick).
model.expr_mod: The remainder of a division of whole numbers.
model.expr_fmod: The remainder of a division of decimal numbers.
model.expr_random: A random whole number from 0 up to one less than the limit.
model.expr_isnan: True when the value is not a number (a sensor that gives no reading).
model.expr_sin: Sine of an angle in radians.
model.expr_cos: Cosine of an angle in radians.
model.expr_tan: Tangent of an angle in radians.
model.expr_asin: Arc sine, the angle in radians.
model.expr_acos: Arc cosine, the angle in radians.
model.expr_atan: Arc tangent, the angle in radians.
model.expr_atan2: The angle in radians of the point x, y, in the right quarter.
model.expr_size: How many items a list has (the # operator); it also gives the length of a text.
model.expr_index: One item of a list, counting from 0.
model.expr_exists: True when a global, a variable, a parameter or a model path exists; use it before reading something that may not be there.
model.expr_exists_default: The value when it exists and a default when it does not, so a missing global never gives an error.
model.expr_vector: A list of n copies of one value.
model.expr_fileexists: True when a file exists on the SD card.
model.expr_null: The value of something that has no value, for example no file loaded.
model.expr_iterations: Inside a while loop of a macro, how many times it has already run.
model.expr_result: The result of the last command of a macro: 0 is success, 1 a warning, 2 an error.
model.expr_param: A parameter the macro was called with (M98 P"file" S5 gives param.S).
model.expr_global: A global variable, created with global name = value.
model.expr_var: A variable local to the macro, created with var name = value.
model.expr_path: Any path of the object model; use the Paths tab to pick one.
model.expr_axis: Where an axis is, in machine coordinates.
model.expr_heater: The current temperature of a heater.
model.expr_tool: The active temperature of a tool.
model.expr_job: The layer the job is printing; empty when there is no job.
model.expr_braces: Curly braces put the value of an expression into a G-code line.
model.expr_set: Changes a global variable from an expression.
model.expr_if: Runs the lines under it only when the condition is true.
model.recipe_heater_over_what: True when this heater is hotter than 60 degrees; change the number.
model.recipe_any_hot: Any of two heaters too hot
model.recipe_any_hot_what: True when the hotter of the two first heaters is above 60 degrees.
model.recipe_bed_temperature_what: The current temperature of the first bed heater, found through the model.
model.recipe_axis_inside_what: True when the first axis is between its minimum and its maximum.
model.recipe_axes_homed_what: True when the first two axes have been homed.
model.recipe_job_layer: Is a job running, and which layer
model.recipe_job_layer_what: Says the layer while a job is processing and that there is no job otherwise.
model.recipe_uptime_hours_what: The uptime of the board in whole hours.
model.recipe_global_default: A global, or a default if it does not exist
model.recipe_global_default_what: The value of a global when it exists and 0 when it does not, so it never gives an error.
model.recipes_none: No recipe fits the model of this board yet.
model.saved_none: Nothing kept yet. Tap the star under the field to keep an expression.
model.saved_full: The list is full (30). Remove one to keep another.
model.error_generic: The board could not evaluate this expression.
model.error_generic_hint: Read the board text below and check the expression piece by piece, starting with the paths.
model.error_name_hint: Check the spelling in the Paths tab. A global, variable or parameter that may not exist must be read with exists(), for example exists(global.x) ? global.x : 0.
model.error_function: The board does not know that function.
model.error_function_hint: See the Angles, Math and Lists groups of the catalog; this firmware only has the functions listed there.
model.error_operator: An operator is wrong or in the wrong place.
model.error_operator_hint: Operators are in the Operators group: use = to compare (not ==), && for and, the doubled vertical bar for or, ^ to join text.
model.error_index: A list position does not exist.
model.error_index_hint: Positions start at 0. Count the items first with # (for example #move.axes) and keep the position below that number.
model.error_type: A value is of the wrong type for this operation.
model.error_type_hint: Compare numbers with numbers and text with text. To mix a number into a text use ^, for example "Layer " ^ job.layer.
model.error_divide_hint: Guard the divisor, for example b = 0 ? 0 : a / b.
model.error_quote_hint: Texts go between double quotes: close the quote you opened.
model.error_syntax: The expression is not well formed.
model.error_syntax_hint: Check that every bracket is closed, that there is a value on both sides of each operator and that nothing is left over at the end.
model.lint_unbalanced: The bracket {what} is not closed or has no pair.
model.lint_quote: A text is open: close the double quote.
model.lint_global_missing: global.{what} does not exist on the board now. Read it with exists(global.{what}) ? global.{what} : 0.
model.live_help: Evaluates the expression again and again, like the watch list, one call at a time. It stops by itself after a number of runs so the board is never flooded.
model.live_stopped_invalid: Stopped: the expression is no longer valid.
model.live_stopped_limit: Stopped after {max} runs. Start it again to keep going.
model.live_stopped_error: Stopped: the board answered with an error.
model.live_limit_standalone: On a standalone Duet it waits at least 5 s between runs and stops after 60.
model.live_limit_extras: With SBC mode it waits at least 2 s between runs and stops after 600.
model.dict_move_axis_letter: The letter of the axis (X, Y, Z, U...). Axes are created and named with M584 in config.g.
model.dict_move_axis_user_pos: Where the axis is in the current coordinate system (workplace offsets and tool offsets applied). Moves change it; G92 redefines it without moving.
model.dict_move_axis_machine_pos: Where the axis is in machine coordinates, before any offset. Reported by the firmware; it changes only by moving the axis.
model.dict_move_axis_homed: True when the position of the axis is known (it was homed). Homing with G28 sets it; releasing the motors with M18 clears it.
model.dict_move_axis_min: The lowest position the axis may reach (software limit). Set with M208 S1 in config.g.
model.dict_move_axis_max: The highest position the axis may reach (software limit, also the length of the axis). Set with M208 in config.g.
model.dict_move_axis_speed: The top speed of the axis. M203 sets it (the command takes mm per minute, the model reports mm per second).
model.dict_move_axis_accel: The acceleration of the axis. Set with M201.
model.dict_move_axis_jerk: The instant speed change the axis allows at a corner. Set with M205 (mm per minute in the command).
model.dict_move_axis_current: The motor current of the axis driver. Set with M906; keep it under what the motor and the driver allow.
model.dict_move_axis_steps: Steps the driver sends for one millimetre of travel. Set with M92; a wrong value scales every move.
model.dict_move_axis_microstep: Microstepping of the axis (16 means 1/16 step). Set with M350.
model.dict_move_axis_interp: True when the driver interpolates the microsteps to 256. Set with M350 I1.
model.dict_move_axis_drives: The driver numbers that move this axis. Set with M584 in config.g.
model.dict_move_axis_visible: False for an axis kept out of the interface (a hidden axis). Set with M584 in config.g.
model.dict_move_axis_workplace: The offset of this axis for one workplace (G54 is 0, G55 is 1...). G10 L2 sets it, G10 L20 sets it from the current position.
model.dict_move_axis_babystep: The live correction added to the position (babystepping). M290 changes it while a job runs.
model.dict_move_axis_other: One axis of the machine. Its fields are listed below it.
model.dict_move_extruder_factor: The extrusion multiplier of this extruder (1 is 100 percent). M221 sets it.
model.dict_move_extruder_pa: Pressure advance of the extruder in seconds. Set with M572; 0 turns it off.
model.dict_move_extruder_nonlinear: The non-linear extrusion coefficients of this extruder. Set with M592.
model.dict_move_extruder_speed: The top feed speed of the extruder. Set with M203 E.
model.dict_move_extruder_accel: The acceleration of the extruder. Set with M201 E.
model.dict_move_extruder_jerk: The instant speed change the extruder allows. Set with M205 E.
model.dict_move_extruder_current: The motor current of the extruder driver. Set with M906 E.
model.dict_move_extruder_steps: Steps the extruder driver sends per millimetre of filament. Set with M92 E.
model.dict_move_extruder_microstep: Microstepping of the extruder. Set with M350 E.
model.dict_move_extruder_driver: The driver that moves this extruder. Set with M584 E in config.g.
model.dict_move_extruder_filament: The name of the filament loaded in this extruder. M701 loads it and M702 unloads it.
model.dict_move_extruder_raw: The raw amount of filament pushed by this extruder, before the extrusion factor. Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_move_speed_factor: The speed override (1 is 100 percent). M220 S sets it in percent.
model.dict_move_current_move: The move being executed now: requested and top speed, acceleration, extrusion rate. Reported by the firmware; it changes with every move.
model.dict_move_compensation_type: The kind of bed compensation in use (none, mesh...). G29 builds or loads a mesh, M561 clears it.
model.dict_move_compensation_fade: The height over the bed above which the mesh correction fades out. Set with M376.
model.dict_move_compensation_file: The height map file in use. G29 S1 loads one, G29 S0 saves one.
model.dict_move_compensation_grid: The grid of points probed for the mesh: limits and spacing. Defined with M557 in config.g.
model.dict_move_compensation_skew: The axis skew correction. Set with M556.
model.dict_move_compensation_other: Bed compensation state reported by the firmware (mesh height map, tilt, skew).
model.dict_move_kinematics: The kinematics of the machine (Cartesian, CoreXY, delta...) and its parameters. Set with M669 in config.g.
model.dict_move_idle_timeout: Seconds without moves before the motors drop to idle current. Set with M84 S.
model.dict_move_idle_factor: The fraction of the motor current kept while idle. Set with M906 I (percent).
model.dict_move_workplace: The workplace in use: 0 is G54, 1 is G55 and so on. Select it with G54 to G59.3.
model.dict_move_print_accel: The acceleration used for moves that extrude. Set with M204 P.
model.dict_move_travel_accel: The acceleration used for travel moves. Set with M204 T.
model.dict_move_virtual_epos: The virtual extruder position, the sum of all extrusion since start. Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_move_shaping: Input shaping (vibration compensation): type, frequency and damping. Set with M593.
model.dict_move_rotation: The coordinate rotation in use (angle and centre). G68 sets it and G69 cancels it.
model.dict_move_limit_axes: True when moves stay inside the axis limits. Set with M564 S.
model.dict_move_no_moves_before_homing: True when moves are refused until the axes are homed. Set with M564 H.
model.dict_move_queue: The state of a motion queue (how many moves wait). Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_heat_current: The temperature the heater sensor reads now. It changes by heating or cooling, not by a command.
model.dict_heat_active: The active target temperature. M104 sets it for a tool heater, M140 for the bed, M141 for the chamber, G10 for a tool.
model.dict_heat_standby: The standby target, used when the tool is not selected. G10 R sets it for a tool.
model.dict_heat_state: The heater state: off, standby, active, fault or tuning. M568 sets it; a fault is cleared with M562.
model.dict_heat_sensor: The number of the temperature sensor this heater reads. Linked with M950 H in config.g.
model.dict_heat_max: The temperature limit of the heater; above it the firmware shuts the heater down. Set with M143 S.
model.dict_heat_min: The lowest temperature the heater accepts as plausible. Below it the sensor is treated as faulty.
model.dict_heat_avg_pwm: The average power the heater has used lately (1 is full power). Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_heat_model: The heating model of the heater: gain, time constant, dead time and PID values. M307 sets it; M303 tunes it automatically.
model.dict_heat_monitors: A heater monitor: a limit and what to do when it is crossed. Set with M143 and M570.
model.dict_heat_tuning: The result of the last heater tuning (M303). Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_heat_bed: The heater number used as bed heater. Assigned with M140 P in config.g; -1 means none.
model.dict_heat_chamber: The heater number used as chamber heater. Assigned with M141 P in config.g; -1 means none.
model.dict_heat_cold_extrude: The minimum temperature to extrude. Set with M302 S; extrusion below it is refused.
model.dict_heat_cold_retract: The minimum temperature to retract. Set with M302 R.
model.dict_fans_requested: The speed the fan was asked to run at (0 to 1). M106 S sets it (0 to 255 or 0 to 1).
model.dict_fans_actual: The speed the fan really runs at now. It may differ from the request (thermostatic control, blip, limits).
model.dict_fans_rpm: Revolutions per minute from the tachometer wire; -1 means the fan has no tachometer. Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_fans_name: The name of the fan. M106 C sets it.
model.dict_fans_min: The lowest speed the fan is allowed to run at. M106 L sets it.
model.dict_fans_max: The highest speed the fan is allowed to run at. M106 X sets it.
model.dict_fans_blip: How long the fan runs at full power to start spinning. M106 B sets it.
model.dict_fans_frequency: The PWM frequency of the fan output. M106 Q sets it.
model.dict_fans_thermostatic: Thermostatic control: the heaters or sensors watched and the temperatures that start and fully run the fan. M106 H and T set it.
model.dict_fans_other: One fan output. Its fields are listed below it; it is created with M950 F in config.g.
model.dict_tools_active: The active temperature of each heater of the tool. G10 S sets it; M104 sets it for the selected tool.
model.dict_tools_standby: The standby temperature of each heater of the tool. G10 R sets it.
model.dict_tools_state: The tool state: active, standby or off. A T command selects a tool; M568 sets the state of a tool.
model.dict_tools_offsets: The offset of the tool on each axis. G10 P X Y Z sets it.
model.dict_tools_heaters: The heater numbers the tool uses. Defined with M563 H.
model.dict_tools_extruders: The extruder drives the tool uses. Defined with M563 D.
model.dict_tools_fans: The fans the tool controls. Defined with M563 F.
model.dict_tools_name: The name of the tool. Defined with M563 S.
model.dict_tools_number: The number of the tool, the one T uses to select it. Defined with M563 P.
model.dict_tools_axes: The axes the tool moves. Defined with M563 X.
model.dict_tools_mix: The mixing ratio of each extruder of the tool. M567 sets it.
model.dict_tools_spindle: The spindle number the tool uses. Defined with M563 R.
model.dict_tools_retraction: Firmware retraction of the tool: length, speeds and Z hop. M207 sets it.
model.dict_tools_is_retracted: True while the filament is retracted. G10 retracts and G11 recovers.
model.dict_sensors_analog_reading: The last reading of the temperature sensor. A very high or very low value means a sensor fault.
model.dict_sensors_analog_name: The name of the sensor. Set with M308 A.
model.dict_sensors_analog_type: The kind of sensor (thermistor, PT1000, thermocouple...). Set with M308 Y or S in config.g.
model.dict_sensors_analog_state: The health of the sensor: ok, shortCircuit, openCircuit, tooHigh, tooLow and so on. Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_sensors_analog_params: A parameter of the sensor (beta, C, R25, port, adjustments). Set with M308 in config.g.
model.dict_sensors_endstop_triggered: True while the endstop is pressed. It follows the switch; check it with M119.
model.dict_sensors_endstop_config: The endstop setup: which end, which kind. Set with M574 in config.g.
model.dict_sensors_probe_value: The current reading of the probe. 1000 is the usual value when it is triggered on a Z probe.
model.dict_sensors_probe_trigger: The height of the nozzle when the probe triggers. G31 Z sets it.
model.dict_sensors_probe_offsets: The X and Y offset of the probe from the nozzle. G31 X Y sets it.
model.dict_sensors_probe_threshold: The value at which the probe counts as triggered. G31 P sets it.
model.dict_sensors_probe_config: The probe setup: type, speeds, dive height, tolerance. Set with M558 in config.g.
model.dict_sensors_filament_status: The filament monitor status: ok, noFilament, tooLittleMovement, tooMuchMovement, sensorError and so on. Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_sensors_filament_config: The filament monitor setup: type, enabled, tolerances. Set with M591 in config.g.
model.dict_sensors_gpin: The value of a general purpose input (0 or 1, or an analog reading). Follows the pin; defined with M950 J.
model.dict_boards_firmware: The firmware version of the board. It changes only by updating the firmware (M997).
model.dict_boards_firmware_date: The build date of the firmware.
model.dict_boards_unique_id: The unique serial identifier of the board.
model.dict_boards_can_address: The CAN bus address of the board. The main board is 0; expansion boards get theirs from their own setup.
model.dict_boards_mcu_temp: The temperature of the processor: current, lowest and highest seen. A high value means poor cooling.
model.dict_boards_vin: The supply voltage: current, lowest and highest seen. Low values hint at a weak supply or a bad connector.
model.dict_boards_v12: The voltage of the 12 V rail: current, lowest and highest seen.
model.dict_boards_max_motors: How many stepper drivers the board has.
model.dict_boards_max_heaters: How many heater outputs the board has.
model.dict_boards_drivers: The state of a stepper driver: stall, overtemperature, open load or short flags. Reported by the driver chip; M122 prints the same in the diagnostics.
model.dict_boards_other: A field of the board reported by the firmware.
model.dict_state_status: What the machine is doing: idle, processing, paused, halted, off and so on. It follows the machine, not a command. M999 resets a halted board.
model.dict_state_current_tool: The selected tool number; -1 means none. A T command selects it.
model.dict_state_next_tool: The tool that will be selected next, during a tool change.
model.dict_state_previous_tool: The tool that was selected before the current one.
model.dict_state_machine_mode: The mode of the machine: FFF, Laser or CNC. M451 selects FFF, M452 laser and M453 CNC.
model.dict_state_time: The date and time of the board. M905 sets it.
model.dict_state_atx: True when the ATX power supply is on. M80 turns it on and M81 turns it off.
model.dict_state_gpout: The output level of a general purpose output (0 to 1). M42 sets it.
model.dict_state_display_message: The message shown on the display. M117 sets it.
model.dict_state_log_file: The log file in use, or empty. M929 starts and stops logging.
model.dict_state_message_box: A message box waiting for an answer. M291 shows it and M292 acknowledges it.
model.dict_state_restore_points: A saved restore point (position and feed rate). M120 saves one and M121 restores it.
model.dict_state_power_fail: The G-code run when the power fails. M911 sets it.
model.dict_state_startup_error: The error that stopped the start-up, if any. Fix the line it names in config.g.
model.dict_state_laser_pwm: The laser power now (0 to 1) when in laser mode.
model.dict_state_dsf_version: The version of the software on the single board computer that drives the board, when there is one.
model.dict_state_other: A field of the machine state reported by the firmware.
model.dict_job_file: What the G-code file says about itself (name, size, layers, filament, slicer). Read from the file when a job starts; M23 selects the file.
model.dict_job_file_position: How far into the file the job is, in bytes. It advances by itself; M26 moves it.
model.dict_job_duration: Seconds since the job started, without the paused time.
model.dict_job_times_left: Estimated time left, by file progress, by filament use or by the slicer estimate.
model.dict_job_last_file: The name of the last file that ran.
model.dict_job_other: A field of the job. M32 starts a file, M25 pauses it and M24 resumes it.
model.dict_network_hostname: The host name of the machine on the network. Set with M550 P.
model.dict_network_name: The display name of the machine. Set with M550 P.
model.dict_network_cors: The site allowed to call the machine from a browser (CORS). Set with M586 C.
model.dict_network_iface_state: The state of the network interface: disabled, connected, active and so on. M552 S turns it on or off.
model.dict_network_iface_ip: The IP address the interface uses now. A fixed one is set with M552 P.
model.dict_network_iface_configured_ip: The IP address asked for in the configuration; 0.0.0.0 means DHCP. Set with M552 P.
model.dict_network_iface_gateway: The gateway address. Set with M554.
model.dict_network_iface_subnet: The subnet mask. Set with M552 S.
model.dict_network_iface_mac: The hardware address of the interface. M540 sets a custom one.
model.dict_network_iface_ssid: The wireless network the interface is joined to. Stored with M587 and joined with M552.
model.dict_network_iface_other: A field of the network interface reported by the firmware.
model.dict_directories_any: A folder the firmware reads or writes (gcodes, macros, system, filaments, web). Set with M505 P.
model.dict_limits_any: A limit built into the firmware (how many axes, heaters, fans, tools and so on). It cannot be changed without another firmware build.
model.dict_volumes_mounted: True when the card or drive is mounted and readable. M21 mounts it and M22 releases it.
model.dict_volumes_free: Free space of the card or drive.
model.dict_volumes_capacity: Total size of the card or drive.
model.dict_volumes_open_files: How many files are open on the card or drive.
model.dict_volumes_speed: The transfer speed of the card or drive, in bytes per second.
model.dict_volumes_other: A field of the card or drive reported by the firmware.
model.dict_inputs_axes_relative: True when moves are relative. G91 selects relative and G90 absolute.
model.dict_inputs_drives_relative: True when extrusion is relative. M83 selects relative and M82 absolute.
model.dict_inputs_distance_unit: The length unit of this input: mm or inch. G21 selects mm and G20 inches.
model.dict_inputs_feed_rate: The feed rate this input will use for the next move. The F word sets it.
model.dict_inputs_volumetric: True when extrusion is given as volume. M200 sets the filament diameter and turns it on.
model.dict_inputs_state: What this G-code input is doing: idle, active, waiting and so on.
model.dict_inputs_other: A field of a G-code input (the web, a file, a macro, the serial line). Reported by the firmware.
model.dict_spindles_active: The requested spindle speed. M3 starts it clockwise, M4 counter-clockwise and M5 stops it.
model.dict_spindles_current: The speed the spindle runs at now.
model.dict_spindles_state: The spindle state: stopped, forward or reverse. M3, M4 and M5 change it.
model.dict_spindles_range: The lowest spindle speed. The limits are set with M950 R in config.g.
model.dict_spindles_other: A field of the spindle reported by the firmware.
model.dict_global_any: A global variable of the machine. It is created with global and changed with set, both meta commands of RepRapFirmware 3.4 and newer; it lasts until restart unless a macro recreates it.
model.dict_plugins_any: What a plugin reports about itself (name, version, process). Plugins are installed and started from the web interface settings.
model.dict_sbc_any: Information about the single board computer that drives the board. It exists only in SBC mode.
model.dict_messages_any: A message the machine sent (time, kind and text). The kind tells success, warning or error.
model.dict_help_what: A short description of the selected path of the object model: what it is, its unit, whether it can be changed and with which command.
model.dict_help_why: The model gives names, not explanations. This tells you what a value is for and how to change it without searching the documentation.
model.dict_help_missing: Without it you only see the raw name and value. A path that is not described here simply shows no description; it is still readable and watchable as usual.
model.dict_help_how: Select any path. The block shows the meaning, the unit, how it changes and the command to use. To try a command, copy it from the path helper or the expression tester.
model.dict_unknown: This path has no description in the dictionary. It may be new in your firmware or specific to a plugin.
model.dict_unavailable: This board reports RRF {current}, older than {version}: the path is probably not there.
model.dict_change_config: Yes, set at start-up in config.g
model.diag_help_what: A check of the live model for anything abnormal: drivers in trouble, supply voltages, heaters and sensors, filament monitors, cards, network, processor temperature, machine state, error messages and plugins.
model.diag_help_why: Problems show up in many branches of the model. This gathers them in one place, errors first, so you do not have to open each card to find out something is wrong.
model.diag_help_missing: Without it you would have to look at each card by eye. A check whose branch the model does not have is skipped and not counted, so an all-clear only covers what was really checked.
model.diag_help_how: Read the list from the top. Tap a line to see what it means and what to check, and Open to jump to the value in the technical tree. The list follows the model every second.
model.diag_all_clear: All clear: {n} checks ran and nothing is wrong.
model.diag_no_data: Nothing to check yet: the model has not reported the branches the checks read.
model.diag_what_it_means: What it means and what to check
model.diag_status_halted_help: The firmware stopped everything after a serious problem (heater fault, emergency stop, driver error, M112). Read the messages and the console for the cause, fix it, then send M999 to reset the board.
model.diag_startup_error_help: The board found a problem while reading its configuration. The named line did not run, so part of the machine may be unconfigured. Fix that line in config.g (or the macro it names) and restart.
model.diag_status_off_help: The main power is off, so heaters and motors cannot work. Turn the power on (M80, or the power button in the interface). If you did not expect it, check the supply and the emergency stop.
model.diag_driver_shutdown_help: The driver chip got too hot and switched itself off. Check the motor current (M906), the cooling of the board and the ambient temperature; the driver recovers when it cools down.
model.diag_driver_short_help: The driver detected a short in the motor wiring or the motor. Switch the power off and check the cable, the connector and the motor windings before using that axis again.
model.diag_driver_error_help: The driver reports a fault. Run M122 and read the line of that driver for the details, then check the wiring, the supply and the motor current.
model.diag_driver_overtemp_help: The driver is getting hot and may shut down soon. Lower the motor current (M906), improve the airflow or add a heatsink fan.
model.diag_driver_open_load_help: No motor seems to be connected to that driver, or one coil is open. Check the motor cable and connector. It is normal for a driver with nothing attached.
model.diag_driver_stall_help: The driver sensed that the motor lost steps or hit an obstacle. It is expected during sensorless homing (M915). Otherwise check for a jam, a loose belt or too low a motor current.
model.diag_vin_low: Board {board}: supply voltage is low, {v} V.
model.diag_vin_low_help: The supply is under 11.5 V. Motors and heaters may misbehave and the board can reset. Check the power supply, its load and the cable and connectors; a long thin cable drops voltage.
model.diag_vin_high: Board {board}: supply voltage is high, {v} V.
model.diag_vin_high_help: The supply is over 26 V, near the limit of many boards. A supply that is too high can damage the board and the drivers. Check the supply setting and the board specification.
model.diag_v12_low: Board {board}: the 12 V rail is low, {v} V.
model.diag_v12_low_help: The 12 V rail that feeds the fans and the logic is under 11 V. Check the supply and whatever is connected to the 12 V outputs; a short there can pull it down.
model.diag_v12_high: Board {board}: the 12 V rail is high, {v} V.
model.diag_v12_high_help: The 12 V rail is over 13 V. Fans and sensors on it may be stressed. Check the supply and the board regulator.
model.diag_mcu_critical: Board {board}: the processor is at {v} C.
model.diag_mcu_critical_help: The processor is close to its maximum temperature. Stop the job and let it cool; check the airflow, the fan and the room temperature.
model.diag_mcu_hot: Board {board}: the processor is warm, {v} C.
model.diag_mcu_hot_help: A processor above 70 C usually means poor ventilation or a hot enclosure. Check that the board fan runs and that the air can flow.
model.diag_heater_fault_help: The firmware switched this heater off because of a problem (temperature rose too slowly or too fast, a sensor fault). Find the cause in the messages, fix it and clear the fault with M562 P{n}. Do not leave the heater on without checking.
model.diag_heater_offline_help: The heater is on an expansion board that is not answering. Check the CAN cable and the power of that board.
model.diag_heater_over_max: Heater {n} reads {v} C, above its limit of {max} C.
model.diag_heater_over_max_help: The temperature is over the limit set with M143. The firmware normally shuts the heater down; if it did not, switch it off at once and check the heater and the sensor.
model.diag_sensor_fault_help: The sensor is not giving a valid reading (open circuit, short, out of range). The heater using it is switched off for safety. Check the sensor wire and connector.
model.diag_filament_error_help: The monitor saw less or more filament movement than expected, or the sensor failed. Check for a clog, a tangled spool, a slipping extruder or a loose sensor cable.
model.diag_filament_warning_help: The monitor reports no filament or no data. Load filament or check that the sensor is connected.
model.diag_volume_unmounted_help: The card or drive cannot be read. Volume 0 is the card with the configuration and the macros: without it the board cannot start jobs or run macros. Check that the card is inserted and send M21 to mount it.
model.diag_network_down_help: The interface is disabled or has no link, so the web interface may be unreachable from other devices. Check the cable or the Wi-Fi settings; M552 S1 turns the network on. Ignore it if you switched it off on purpose.
model.diag_messages_error_help: The machine sent error messages that are still in the list. Open the messages or the console to read them in full; they usually name the command or the file that failed.
model.diag_plugin_stopped: Plugin {name} has a process on the board but it is not running.
model.diag_plugin_stopped_help: The plugin starts a program on the single board computer and that program is not running. It may be stopped on purpose; if not, start it in Settings, Plugins and read its log.
model.vs_mode_help: Names looks in the paths and values; Values looks only at what the values are, over the whole model.
model.vs_help_what: A second way to search the flat list. Instead of looking for a name, it finds every path of the whole model whose value matches what you type.
model.vs_help_why: Useful when you know what the value looks like but not where it lives: every temperature above 60, every value that is true, everything that says error, every empty text.
model.vs_help_missing: Without it you can only filter by name, or scan the list by eye. In Names mode the box still searches names and values together as before.
model.vs_help_how: Switch to Values and type: a word (contains), "idle" or =idle (equals), !=0 (different), >30 >=30 <5 <=5 (numbers), 10..20 (between), true, false, null, empty. The line below says how the text was read.
model.vs_read_number_ge: Numbers greater than or equal to {n}
model.vs_read_number_le: Numbers less than or equal to {n}
model.vs_read_empty: Empty values (a blank text, an empty list or object)
model.vs_read_invalid: Not understood: {text}. Write an operator and a number, like >30.
model.usage_intro: Press the button to read your macros. It takes a few seconds and nothing is changed on the machine.
model.usage_options_show_hint: These filters apply to the By global tab.
model.usage_only_file: Only globals used by this file
model.usage_card_problems_say: A file reads them and nobody creates them. They fail when they run.
model.usage_card_problems_none: None. Everything a file reads gets created.
model.usage_card_check_say: Maybe a problem: created in a folder not read, or nobody reads them.
model.usage_set_cards_what: Three cards that sort the globals: problems (a file reads one and nobody creates it), to check (it may be created in a folder not read, or nobody reads it) and everything.
model.usage_set_cards_why: The problems are what fails when a macro runs, so they come first; the rest is for a second look.
model.usage_set_cards_missing: You would have to go through every global to find the ones that fail.
model.usage_set_cards_help: Click a card to filter the list below. Searching or picking a file shows everything; clearing it goes back to the card that matters.
model.usage_say_maybe: Read in {files}; it may be created in a folder not read yet
model.usage_say_live_written: Exists on the machine, written in {files}, nobody reads it
model.usage_say_live: Exists on the machine, no file uses it
model.usage_clear_text: Every global a file reads is created by some file or exists on the machine.
model.usage_no_match_hint: Try a shorter name or clear the search.
model.usage_byfile_empty: No file has been read yet.
model.usage_banner_reason: {n} folders could create a global and were left out, so some problems may not be real:
model.recipes_share_show_newer: Show {n} recipes that need a newer firmware
model.recipes_share_hide_newer: Hide the recipes that need a newer firmware
model.recipes_share_none_match: No recipe matches what you typed.
model.recipes_share_contribute: Add your own recipe to the plugin
model.recipes_share_contribute_what: The recipes marked Community are JSON files in the public repository of the plugin, bundled into it when a version is built; anyone can propose one.
model.recipes_share_contribute_why: So a formula that works in your workshop helps the next person, with your name on it.
model.recipes_share_contribute_missing: Nothing changes here: the plugin works the same with or without community recipes, and this page never connects to the internet.
model.recipes_share_contribute_help: Tap Share on a saved formula or on a recipe: the dialog builds the file, checks it and shows the steps. The guide of the repository explains the format.
model.recipes_share_guide_link: Guide to contribute a recipe (opens the repository)
model.recipes_share_lead: Turns the formula into a recipe file for the repository of the plugin. Nothing is sent by this page: you copy or download the file and publish it yourself.
model.recipes_share_private_note: The file holds only what you see here. An address, a host name, a file path of your PC or a value read from the board is refused.
model.recipes_share_id_what: A short name in lower case letters, digits and hyphens: it is the name of the file, id.json.
model.recipes_share_id_why: To tell one recipe from another: two recipes cannot share an identifier.
model.recipes_share_id_missing: The file cannot be made without it.
model.recipes_share_id_help: Say what it answers, as in heater-above-limit. It is suggested from the title; change it if you like.
model.recipes_share_name_what: The line the Recipes tab shows for it, in English; the Spanish one is optional.
model.recipes_share_name_why: It is how people find the recipe in the list and in the search.
model.recipes_share_name_missing: A recipe without an English title is refused by the check.
model.recipes_share_name_help: One short sentence that says what it answers, up to 80 characters.
model.recipes_share_description_what: What the recipe tells and when it is useful, in English; the Spanish one is optional.
model.recipes_share_description_why: So someone who did not write it knows what the numbers mean and when to use it.
model.recipes_share_description_missing: A recipe without an English description is refused by the check.
model.recipes_share_description_help: Two or three sentences, up to 300 characters: what it is true for, which number to change, what to watch out for.
model.recipes_share_kind_what: What the recipe gives: a value, a true or false, a path to read with M409, or a text to show.
model.recipes_share_kind_why: The tab loads it in the right mode and the check knows what answer to expect.
model.recipes_share_kind_missing: It is guessed from the formula; a wrong kind is refused when the example does not fit it.
model.recipes_share_kind_help: A comparison is a condition; a number or a list is an expression; a line with ^ that builds a text is a text; a path is M409.
model.recipes_share_template_what: The expression as it will be loaded. A part the person must adapt is a blank: a plain name in lower case between the less-than and greater-than signs, the way the catalog of the builder writes its blanks.
model.recipes_share_template_why: A blank makes the recipe work on any machine: the person fills it when the recipe is loaded.
model.recipes_share_template_missing: Without blanks the recipe carries your numbers and indexes; it still works, but only as is.
model.recipes_share_template_help: Replace a heater number, a limit or a global name by a blank named heater, limit or name, between the less-than and greater-than signs. Each blank then gets its own line below.
model.recipes_share_holes_row_what: One line per blank of the formula: its type and what goes in it.
model.recipes_share_holes_row_why: The person who loads the recipe sees what each blank expects.
model.recipes_share_holes_row_missing: A blank without a description is refused by the check.
model.recipes_share_holes_row_help: Say in English what to put and where to find it, as in: the number of the heater in heat.heaters.
model.recipes_share_since_what: The oldest firmware the formula works on.
model.recipes_share_since_why: On an older board the Recipes tab hides it, marked needs RRF x.y, instead of giving an error.
model.recipes_share_since_missing: The check refuses a recipe without it.
model.recipes_share_since_help: 3.1 for a plain expression or condition, 3.3 when it uses a global or exists(), 3.5 for vector(). It is not read from your board.
model.recipes_share_sample_row_what: The formula with every blank filled, and the kind of answer it gives.
model.recipes_share_sample_row_why: People can load the example as it is and see what to expect; the check uses it to see that the blanks are filled.
model.recipes_share_sample_row_missing: The check refuses a recipe without an example.
model.recipes_share_sample_row_help: Fill the blanks with values that work on a common machine; a condition always answers true or false.
model.recipes_share_filled: The formula with the blanks filled
model.recipes_share_author_what: Your GitHub user name, shown next to the recipe. Optional.
model.recipes_share_author_why: Credit, and a way to ask you about it.
model.recipes_share_author_missing: The recipe is shown without a name.
model.recipes_share_author_help: Only the user name, without the at sign.
model.recipes_share_tags_what: Short words to search by: heaters, fans, safety. Optional, up to 8.
model.recipes_share_tags_why: The search of the Recipes tab finds them.
model.recipes_share_tags_missing: The recipe is found by its title and formula only.
model.recipes_share_tags_help: Lower case words separated by commas.
model.recipes_share_ready: The recipe is ready: a valid file with no private data.
model.recipes_share_publish_what: The file goes to the public repository of the plugin on GitHub as a pull request or an issue, made by you from your browser.
model.recipes_share_publish_why: When the maintainer merges it, it comes with the next version of the plugin, marked Community with your name.
model.recipes_share_publish_missing: The recipe stays in this browser only.
model.recipes_share_publish_help: Copy or download the file, then follow the steps. The pre-filled links open GitHub with the file already in place; they are offered only when the file is short.
model.recipes_share_copy_failed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it by hand.
model.recipes_share_download_failed: The browser did not allow the download: copy the text instead.
model.recipes_share_link_long: The file is too long for a pre-filled link: download it and attach it.
model.recipes_share_step_2: On GitHub, in the repository of the plugin, open the folder {dir}, choose Add file, Create new file, paste the text with the same name and choose Propose new file: GitHub makes the pull request for you (it needs a GitHub account). Or open an issue and paste the file in it.
model.recipes_share_step_3: The maintainer reviews it. When it is merged, the recipe comes with the next version of the plugin.
model.recipes_share_import: Bring a recipe file into your saved formulas
model.recipes_share_import_what: A recipe file (the same JSON the repository takes) pasted or chosen from your PC, checked and added to the saved formulas of this browser.
model.recipes_share_import_why: To try a recipe someone sent you, or one from the repository, before it comes with a version of the plugin.
model.recipes_share_import_missing: You can still type the formula by hand.
model.recipes_share_import_help: Paste the text or choose the file; the check runs at once. When it passes, Add to saved keeps the formula with its blanks to fill.
model.recipes_share_import_paste: Paste the text of a recipe file
model.recipes_share_import_added: Added to your saved formulas as {name}.
model.recipes_share_import_full: Your saved list is full (30): remove one first.
model.recipes_share_import_read_failed: The file could not be read.
model.recipes_share_problem_not_object: The text is not a recipe (a JSON object is expected).
model.recipes_share_problem_unknown_field: {field}: the field {what} is not part of a recipe.
model.recipes_share_problem_private: {field} carries private data ({what}): take it out.
model.recipes_share_problem_unknown_lang: {field}: the language {what} is not en or es.
model.recipes_share_problem_id_format: The identifier must be lower case letters, digits and hyphens.
